issues.description: Method Farm.singFarmSongVerse: the problem statement UML and the template define this helper as private, while the solution implements it as protected. Specifically, the UML lists singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal) as a private method (problem_statement.md line 19), the template declares a private method signature (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 18: private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), and the solution declares it as protected (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 33: protected void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)). This visibility mismatch (private vs protected) can confuse students about whether the helper should be accessible to subclasses or tests and whether they should implement it as private or protected.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution method to private to match the UML/template, or update the UML and the template to declare the method as protected (and adjust the template signature accordingly). Ensure the chosen visibility is documented in the problem statement so students know the intended access level.

issues.description: Method Farm.singFarmSongVerse parameter list differs between artifacts: the UML (problem_statement.md line 19) and the solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 33) expect a single parameter of type Animal (singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)), but the template's method signature omits the parameter (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 18: private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)). The commented-out parameter in the template creates an inconsistency about the intended signature and may confuse students or tests that expect the method to accept an Animal argument.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML and solution by giving singFarmSongVerse the Animal parameter in the template signature (e.g., private/protected void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)). If the intention is to have no parameter, update the UML and the solution accordingly. Prefer adding the parameter to the template so the signature is consistent and students can implement the method as shown in the UML and solution.
